definition: Counteract means to act against something and cancel out its effect.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word counteract. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know counteract should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: A spoonful of honey counteracts the bitterness of the tea without hiding its flavor.
Dampening an effect is milder than counteracting it — the force is softened a little, but most of it still gets through.
Negating an effect goes even further than counteracting it — nothing is left at all, as if the force had never acted.

To counterbalance is to set an equal weight or force against something — static and mechanical, like the counterweight in a crane. To counteract is active and ongoing: you push against a force while it operates, so its effect cancels in real time.

To offset is to balance one thing against another so the totals come out even — an accounting word for gains covering losses. To counteract is more physical and immediate: an opposing action fights a live force directly, cancelling its effect as it happens.

Counteract means to act against something and cancel out its effect.
To counteract the glare that washed out the morning exhibits, the curator hung amber film over the skylights — the sun kept shining, but its effect on the paintings was cancelled.
Counteract is different from 'prevent' or 'undo': it doesn't stop a force from existing or reverse it afterward.
It works against the force in real time, pushing back so the net effect comes out to nothing.
Counteract is the working word of chemists, doctors, and engineers — one force deployed against another so the effect cancels.
Use 'offset' for accounting-flavored balance and 'undo' for repair after the fact.
Its unit-mate neutralize goes to the source and leaves it harmless; counteract leaves the source running and fights its effect to a draw.

By late afternoon, a molecule called adenosine has been collecting in your brain all day, docking into receptors and turning your alertness down notch by notch.
Coffee works because caffeine can counteract that signal while it is being sent.
The caffeine slips into the same receptors and blocks the docking, so the drowsiness message is cancelled in real time — not softened, but stopped as it happens.
Nothing about the adenosine goes away; it keeps arriving, and the caffeine keeps meeting it.
That is why the crash comes later: when the caffeine clears, the accumulated signal lands all at once.
